thread:
incbot: :rotating_light: ALERT: continuous-batching executor reports sustained KV cache growth on prod-cluster-a, auto-scaling triggers suppressed due to quota. Metric: kv_cache_size_bytes +430% in 6m. Possible cause: long-running batches. Paging oncall.
sam-oncall: Ack. I'm on it. pulling logs now.
leo-sre: seeing a lot of `batch_worker` goroutine stuck in `wait_for_timeout` and `apply_kv_page` loops. HTTP 502/504 rate rising ~2.3x. traces: https://logs.redwood/c/cluster-a?q=batch_worker
ash-ml: last model rollout had continuous-batching default change: `max_batch_tokens` bumped from 1024 -> 8192 in a canary tomorrow, but I see it in prod config for cluster-a ?
mike-ops: checking infra automation — there was a config drift during the rollout job. `redwood-serve` trial flag `cbatch_max_batch_tokens` set to 8192 for the canary group; it accidentally targeted prod-cluster-a label. oof.
jenn-csm: we have 2 active customers (AcmeHealth, Nestro) reporting degraded responses on their endpoints. AcmeHealth on Dedicated-42 reports timeouts in their SLO window.
irina-pm: severity? customer-impacting yes -> Sev2 if >1 customer with >1% errors.
sam-oncall: marking Sev2. Begin mitigation steps. Quick plan: 1) throttle continuous batching on cluster-a (set max_num_seqs=1, max_batch_tokens=1024) 2) evict stale KV cache pages (safe eviction script) 3) monitor latency/errors 4) follow up with rollback of stray flag.
leo-sre: agreed. I can push a transient config patch to gate continuous batching. Applying patch via ops API.
leo-sre: ```
# disable wide continuous batches on cluster-a
curl -X POST https://ops-api.internal/v1/clusters/cluster-a/config \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $OPS_TOKEN' \
  -d '{"continuous_batching": {"enabled": true, "max_batch_tokens": 1024, "max_num_seqs": 1, "batch_timeout_ms": 50}}'
``` 
leo-sre: patch applied (deploy id: d9f3c1b). Rolling changes onto live nodes.
deploy-bot: rollout started for config d9f3c1b -> 12/12 nodes in cluster-a (0:00 elapsed)
ash-ml: NOTE: setting `max_num_seqs=1` will reduce KV cache sharing but increase per-request compute. We're trading cost for stability.
mike-ops: running eviction for hot KV pages: `python tools/kv_eviction.py --cluster cluster-a --age-threshold 30m --dry-run=false`
mike-ops: eviction started, immediate frees ~18GiB in first sweep.
leo-sre: metrics: kv_cache_size_bytes -> -28% within 3m of eviction start. error rate down from 2.3% to 0.9% and latency p50 back to baseline.
jenn-csm: AcmeHealth confirms reduced timeouts, Nestro still seeing occasional 504s but improved.
sam-oncall: good. next step: fix config drift root cause and author a safety guard to prevent canary flags from hitting prod labels.
ash-ml: will revert the experimental canary flag in model rollout pipeline. Adding a validation step: deny canary flag targeting prod label explicitly.
irina-pm: please collect customer impact window & affected request IDs for postmortem. Jenn, can you coordinate with CSMs to get the list?
jenn-csm: on it. I'll pull request logs and reach out to account teams.
mike-ops: created PR to enforce label scoping: https://git.internal/r/redwood/infra/+/PR-3214
leo-sre: monitoring: added alert: `cbatch_kv_growth_rate` > 50% over 5m now triggers paging AND a circuit-breaker that forces `continuous_batching.enabled=false` on the affected cluster as automated fallback.
sam-oncall: enabling the circuit-breaker is a good safety net. Is it toggled to manual or auto?
leo-sre: auto for this threshold, with 2-step automated rollback: 1) set enabled=false, 2) notify oncall for manual re-enable.
sam-oncall: good. handoff: I'll be available for 15 more minutes, then switching to leo-sre for overnight oncall. If error rate climbs back above 1.5% escalate to eng-oncall.
leo-sre: taking over at 1963005276. I'll keep the thread updated. Confirmed current status: KV cache stable, error rate 0.7%, rolling back stray flag in pipeline.
sam-oncall: thanks, handing off. :thumbsup:
jenn-csm: customers looped, tickets created: ACME-1283, NEST-421. I'll include sample request_ids and SLA impact timeline.
ash-ml: quick note for postmortem: root cause = config drift that exposed an experimental `max_batch_tokens=8192` in prod; that allowed very large batches to stay open (due to long `batch_timeout_ms` defaults) which caused KV cache to retain more pages per batch and prevented eviction, leading to a memory and perf cliff.
ash-ml: recommended long term: 1) tighter validation on rollout tooling 2) default `max_batch_tokens` cap per cluster tier 3) adaptive batch_timeout based on tail latencies.
leo-sre: capturing logs/traces: https://traces.redwood/trace/1963005123
deploy-bot: config d9f3c1b deployed successfully to all nodes (12/12) at 1963005202
sam-oncall: closing preliminary incident action. Please add notes to incident tracker and schedule postmortem sync with relevant owners.
leo-sre: adding timeline + config diffs to incident doc. assigning follow-ups: infra (PR-3214), ml (rollback validation), sres (alert tuning), csm (customer comms).
jenn-csm: customers happy with interim fix; will plan follow-up comms after postmortem.
leo-sre: end handoff note: leaving monitoring on auto-circuit breaker. If anything regresses, page eng-oncall immediately.
incbot: Incident marked RESOLVED_BY_MITIGATION at 1963005276 (metadata: severity=2, impacted_customers=["AcmeHealth","Nestro"], action=throttle_and_evict).
